what: Station dashboard shows all four cameras (perception webcam plus overhead, left-wrist and right-wrist arm cameras); the MacBook can make Dream calls with those live views.
why: Consolidating after the demo so post-hackathon experiments start from a working station: the same three views Dream's embodiment expects, and one command to send a prompt such as Saleh's water-bottle handover.
details: Arm cameras are pinned to their Jetson USB hub ports and opened as MJPG at 15 fps; raw YUYV from four cameras saturated the shared USB 2.0 hub (right wrist failed, detector fell to 10 fps). With MJPG: all live, detector back to about 24 fps.
Each arm camera is served at /cam/{overhead,wrist_l,wrist_r}.jpg; the --mac dashboard pulls them from the Jetson through the SSH tunnel.

dream_live.py reuses probe.configure / model.prepare (dream-1-beta, the Table 10 runner's checkpoint), sends the three live frames plus both arms' state, and saves the action chunk with an SDK-degree summary. It never actuates. State is measured SDK readings or an explicitly labelled NOMINAL pose.
Removed the superseded MJPEG route and the stale control-center process.
